Comicraft website

The comic-lettering foundry’s home page opens on a full-width comic panel with halftone shading, a speech balloon, and a sunburst background.

Context

The site sells comic-book fonts; its navigation lists Word Balloons, Sound Effects, Character Voices, and Display Fonts. Comicraft.

Observed

  • A bright yellow navigation bar holds the logo “The World’s Greatest Comic Book Fonts!” in red and yellow outlined letters, and menu items in a condensed comic font.
  • The hero is one comic panel: a hippo in a shirt and tie beside a woman on a sofa, drawn with black ink lines.
  • The figures are shaded with visible halftone dots in orange, red, and green.
  • A large white speech balloon with a black outline reads “Thru Thick and Thin?” in hand-lettered type.
  • Behind the panel, an orange sunburst of rays and paint splashes fills the width of the page.
  • A boxed “#5 2026” issue badge and an “Approved by the Comicraft Authority” seal copy comic-cover devices.
  • Below the hero, two flat yellow buttons read “WHAT’S NEW” and “MOST POPULAR” in black italic capitals.

Why it belongs

The halftone dots and heavy outlines are inside the hero image, so the extractor cannot see them: surface.patternShare is 0.06, color.patternShare is 0, and the median CSS border is 1 px. The page is a clear example by the rubric but fails those metrics for that reason.

Shadows cover 14% of boxes but with a 1 px offset and 1 px blur; they are not the hard offset shadows of neo-brutalism.

Borrow

Put the main statement in a speech balloon over the hero image, not in a separate heading.

Use comic-cover furniture, such as an issue number box or a seal, as small secondary badges.
